title: Merge tick/x6j: union three collect.go rewrites without losing a guarantee
description:
Merge tick/x6j into the integration branch. Three wave-4 ticks (gwc, p6b, x6j)
each independently rewrote internal/exec/herdr/collect.go's classify() and the
doc.go status list. gwc and p6b are already merged; x6j conflicts with the
result in 9 places: 5 in collect.go, 2 in doc.go, 2 in harness_test.go.

This is a union in INTENT, not in text — `.tick/learnings.md` already carries
the rule: "Two additions to one file are a union in INTENT, not in text — hand
the resolve to a worker holding the context."

WHAT EACH TICK ADDED, so you can tell a union from a regression:
- gwc: wall-clock enforcement. classify() gained a `wallExceeded bool`
  parameter and the reason constant `reasonWallClockStopped`. A wall-clock stop
  carries the failure class wall_clock_exceeded but does NOT by itself decide a
  verdict — cancelled and no-commits outrank it, and a worker that reported
  before the stop never reaches a failing check.
- p6b: the artifact boundary. classify() gained an `artifactViolations []string`
  parameter and the reason constant `reasonArtifactCommitted`. The backstop sits
  where the local executor puts it, AFTER the tracker-record boundary check.
- x6j: a substrate failure is never a verdict. Its change is at the one place a
  verdict could be minted out of the substrate's silence: no report, no
  cancellation, no settlement any leg recorded means the attempt was never
  answered, so collect REFUSES with a liveness-unknown hold rather than
  answering "the worker failed".

THE RULE THAT DECIDES EVERY CONFLICT: the check order is the LOCAL executor's
own, because it is the collect vocabulary's — the same tick with the same facts
must collect the same verdict on either executor. Read internal/exec/subprocess/
collect.go and keep this file's order identical to it. A re-ordered copy is how
the two executors come to disagree about one attempt with nothing failing.

Do:
1. `git merge --no-ff tick/x6j` on the integration branch and resolve all 9.
2. Keep ALL THREE guarantees. Dropping one to make the file compile is the
   failure mode here; each has its own tests and they must all still pass.
3. classify() ends up with both new parameters and x6j's hold.
4. doc.go's "What is deliberately NOT here" list: gwc, p6b and x6j are all DONE
   now; only 2xu (already merged), 5hz, 7vn and x9x remain outstanding.
5. `make test-short` green — the whole suite, not just this package.
acceptance_criteria: tick/x6j is merged into the integration branch with all 9 conflicts resolved; classify() carries gwc's wallExceeded, p6b's artifactViolations AND x6j's liveness-unknown hold, with the check order identical to internal/exec/subprocess/collect.go; all three ticks' tests pass, none deleted or weakened to make the file compile; doc.go's outstanding list names only 5hz, 7vn and x9x; make test-short green.
